content:
Most students lose sequence marks to careless counting, not hard ideas. One slip on the nth term wrecks a clean answer. So take the free JEE Sequences and Series online test below. It has 15 exam MCQs and scores you at once. Each answer shows the working. Aim for 12 out of 15.

What JEE asks from this chapter

The paper blends AP, GP and special sums. First come nth-term and sum formulas. Then AM, GM and HP links appear. Word problems on growth and decay finish the set.

  • The nth term and the sum of an AP.
  • The nth term and the sum of a GP, finite and infinite.
  • Arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means.
  • Sums of squares, cubes and telescoping series.
  • Growth, decay and bouncing-ball word problems.

Formulas and facts to revise first

  • An AP nth term is a plus (n minus 1) times d, so check n with care.
  • An infinite GP sums to a over (1 minus r) only when the size of r is below 1.
  • For positive numbers AM is at least GM, and equality means they are all equal.
  • The sum of the first n squares is n(n + 1)(2n + 1) over 6.
  • If a, b and c sit in GP, then b squared equals a times c.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Using the infinite-GP sum when the size of r reaches 1 or more.
  • Counting the wrong term, so the 6th slides into the 5th.
  • Swapping AM and GM inside an inequality bound.
  • Forgetting the factor of 2 for return bounces in ball problems.

quiz.title: JEE Sequences and Series Quiz
quiz.intro: Fifteen exam-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: JEE Maths DPP: Sequences and Series

questions.q: Which term of the AP 3, 8, 13, ... is 78?
questions.explanation: With a = 3 and d = 5, set 3 + (n − 1)5 = 78. Solving gives n = 16.

questions.q: A salary starts at 10000 per month with a 500 annual increment. In which year does it reach 15000?
questions.explanation: The salaries form an AP with a = 10000 and d = 500. Setting the nth term to 15000 gives n = 11.

questions.q: Which term of the GP 2, 2√2, 4, ... is 128?
questions.explanation: Here a = 2 and r = √2. Then 2 times (√2) to the power (n − 1) = 128 gives n = 13.

questions.q: Bacteria double every hour, starting at 100. How many are there after 5 hours?
questions.explanation: The count doubles each hour from 100. After 5 hours it is 100 times 2 to the 5th, which is 3200.

questions.q: A ball is dropped from 10 m and bounces to 3/4 of its height each time. The total distance travelled is:
questions.explanation: Total equals 10 plus twice a GP with first term 30/4 and ratio 3/4. That works out to 10 + 60 = 70 metres.

questions.q: Three numbers in GP have product 216 and sum 19. The numbers are:
questions.explanation: The middle term is the cube root of 216, so it is 6. The set is 4, 6, 9 in either order.

questions.q: If a, b, c are in GP, then log a, log b, log c are in:
questions.explanation: In a GP, b squared equals a times c. Taking logs gives 2 log b = log a + log c, the condition for an AP.

questions.q: The arithmetic mean of two positive numbers is 5 and the geometric mean is 4. The numbers are:
questions.explanation: AM = 5 gives a + b = 10, and GM = 4 gives a times b = 16. The roots of x² − 10x + 16 are 8 and 2.
Factor out 4 to get 4 times the sum of the first ten squares. That is 4 times 385, which is 1540.

questions.q: An infinite GP has sum 4 and first term 2. Its common ratio is:
questions.explanation: The sum equals a over (1 − r), so 4 = 2 over (1 − r). Solving gives r = 1/2.

questions.q: The recurring decimal 0.666... equals which fraction?
questions.explanation: Write it as a GP with first term 6/10 and ratio 1/10. The sum is 6/9, which is 2/3.
Each term splits as 1/n minus 1/(n + 1). The middle parts cancel, leaving 1 − 1/10 = 9/10.
The nth term is n(n + 1) over 2. Summing the squares and the linear part gives n(n + 1)(n + 2) over 6.

questions.q: An infinite GP has sum 3 and the sum of squares of its terms is 9/2. The common ratio is:
questions.explanation: From the two sums, 2(1 − r) = 1 + r. Solving gives r = 1/3.

questions.q: For positive reals x, y, z, the minimum value of (x+y)(y+z)(z+x) is:
questions.explanation: Apply AM at least GM to each pair. Multiplying the three bounds gives at least 8xyz.
